The slice site $\mathcal C/U$ has objects morphisms $V\to U$ of $\mathcal C$, with induced coverings. Denote by $\mathcal O_U$ and $\mathcal F|_U$ the respective restrictions of $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal F$ to this slice. The groups $H^p(U,\mathcal F)$ and $H^p(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal F|_U)$ are the respective right-derived section functors (with $p\ge0$).

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{I}$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}$-module
then $\mathcal{I}|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal{O}_U$-module.
\item For any sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules $\mathcal{F}$ we have
$H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = H^p(\mathcal{C}/U, \mathcal{F}|_U)$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ is a ringed site.
conclusions: For each injective $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal I$, its restriction $\mathcal I|_U$ is an injective $\mathcal O_U$-module.
For each $\mathcal O$-module $\mathcal F$ and $p\ge0$, $H^p(U,\mathcal F)\cong H^p(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal F|_U)$.

semantic_review_note: For slice site C/U, restriction of an injective O-module stays injective over O_U, and cohomology of the object U agrees with cohomology of restricted F on the slice. Both separate assertions and derived cohomology interpretation retained.

\label{lemma-kill-cohomology-class-on-covering}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules.
Let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $n > 0$ and let $\xi \in H^n(U, \mathcal{F})$.
Then there exists a covering $\{U_i \to U\}$ of $\mathcal{C}$
such that $\xi|_{U_i} = 0$ for all $i \in I$.

For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ of modules on a ringed site and a morphism $V\to U$, restriction of sections of an injective resolution induces the natural map $H^n(U,\mathcal F)\to H^n(V,\mathcal F)$; write the image of $\xi$ as $\xi|_V$.

conclusions: There is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ such that $\xi|_{U_i}=0$ for every $i$.

\label{lemma-higher-direct-images}
Let $f : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
For any $\mathcal{F} \in \Ob(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}))$
the sheaf $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is the sheaf associated to the
presheaf
$$
V \longmapsto H^i(u(V), \mathcal{F})
$$

final_content.statement:
For a morphism of ringed sites $f$ corresponding to a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, the sheaf $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is the $i$th right derived direct image of the sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-modules $\mathcal F$; the presheaf below is on $\mathcal D$.

Let $f : (\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}) \to
(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{O}_\mathcal{D})$ be a morphism of ringed sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
For any $\mathcal{F} \in \Ob(\textit{Mod}(\mathcal{O}_\mathcal{C}))$
the sheaf $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$ is the sheaf associated to the
presheaf
$$
V \longmapsto H^i(u(V), \mathcal{F})
$$
hypotheses: $f:(\mathcal C,\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\mathcal D,\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ is a morphism of ringed sites corresponding to a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$.
$\mathcal F$ is an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module and $i\ge0$.
conclusions: $R^if_*\mathcal F$ is canonically the sheafification of the presheaf $V\mapsto H^i(u(V),\mathcal F)$ on $\mathcal D$.

semantic_review_note: The higher direct image R^i f_*F is the sheafification on D of the presheaf V↦H^i(u(V),F), for ringed-site morphism corresponding to continuous u:D→C. The direction and codomain of u and i≥0 are preserved.
